title: No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation
main_claim: For iid nonatomic edge weights on Z^2 with E[min of 4 weights^2] < infinity, almost surely no bigeodesic exists. No limit-shape regularity is assumed, and all bigeodesics are excluded at once, including those whose labels depend on the environment.

issues.description: The whole argument takes Ahlberg–Hoffman as a black box: on one event, every ray from every vertex has an asymptotically linear Busemann function with a label in C, and for each fixed label there is uniqueness, coalescence and backward finiteness. I did not check these source theorems against the AH paper here. This is a dependency, not a demonstrated gap.
issues.evidence: Sec. 2: 'The exact source statements are [AH, Assumption A1, Theorems 2.5–2.6 and 10.8–10.11, and Proposition 4.5]'. Everything in Sections 3–8 uses parts (ii)/(iii).

issues.location: Appendix A, Prop A.3 (replacement for AH Lemma 4.6 / Prop 4.4)
issues.description: The patch for AH's boundary-expectation step reuses two geometric parts of AH without re-proving them: the crossing comparison in eq. (12), and the claim that boundary ergodicity makes the asymptotic planar order deterministic. I re-derived the identity Δ = sum of the two swapped-walk excesses, the zero-increment lemma for a nonnegative stationary additive process (Lemma A.2, which needs no integrability), and the final 2m-separation uniqueness step. All of them check out. The only residual reliance is on those geometric parts of the source.
issues.evidence: Δ(k,l)=(T_H(π_y)-T_H(lz,y))+(T_H(π_x)-T_H(kz,x)) checked from π_x+π_y = T_H(kz,y)+T_H(lz,x). Δ(0,n)/n→0 in probability follows from stationarity and finiteness of Z, without assuming E|Z|<∞.

coverage:
Read every section line by line (Intro, Sections 2–8, Appendix A). Checked each step of the core argument:
- Ray-order lemma: the crossing and Busemann inequalities, including signs.
- Uniform cone confinement: the endpoint-ray offsets are o(n), and the Jordan-domain trapping handles the case where the ray leaves before the bounding rays split.
- Crossing lemma.
- Countability of exceptional labels: the six-ray alternating-color argument for branching, and the disjoint Busemann-value intervals.
- The Fubini argument for the analytic bad set J.
- Half-plane cut transfer: the moving-cut subsequence barrier, exact label identification along two sector directions, and lower tails in W_n.
- Opposite-label coalescence.
- Budget comparison: the bypass via the α and −β comparators, sign conventions, and the separation S.
- Telescoping budget with reverse Fatou.
- One-edge resampling count, including base comparator confinement through the edge endpoints, and E N_e(H) ≤ C(H+1).
- Burton–Keane-style fork count: tree leaves ≥ q+1, disjoint continuations, n/4 usable edges per leaf, giving a cubic-vs-cubic contradiction.
- Same-Busemann corollary.
- Perturbation construction: verified the one-edge density, its second moment 1+(1/p_a+1/p_b)δ², the convergent series, the posterior δ/(p_b+δ), the Abel summation identity, and both Chebyshev bounds.
- Union-metric preservation and the protected near edge outside A_k(R) when l > R_0+1+(R_0+H_0)/s.
- Distinct-label detour: excess → 0 in T*, and a saving of Δ ≥ g in T^{k,R}.
- Final step: the M-dependent separation S(M) is absorbed by refining the partition at fixed M (pointwise finite-set argument), giving p/8 ≤ q_M ≤ lW/M.
I did not independently verify the cited Ahlberg–Hoffman theorems in the original source.
sibling_notes: The family 212 board had no earlier entries visible when I started. Reusable components from this paper: (1) the opposite-coalescence trick for random exceptional labels (half-plane resampling coupling plus Fubini over a countable random set); (2) a translation-equivariant label budget Mq ≤ lW that needs only equal marginals; (3) shared low-to-high raises with δ_h ~ η/(h log h), giving bounded chi-square with divergent gain.
